liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Black Peter** (3 reviews): Reviewer notes this as the first Black Peter and Uncle John's Band; Reviewer finds the arrangement unusual compared with typical versions [6][7][13]
- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Reviewer praises a terrific Dark Star flowing into High Time; Syncopated, faster than usual, about thirty minutes long; organ gives early sound; feedback around 16:05 [6][7][15]
- **Good Morning Little Schoolgirl** (1 review): Pigpen ends it with an ad-lib about being thirteen years old, after a long pause [6]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Described as the first recording of the song; band had learned it only days earlier [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Introduction + Invitation to what would become Altamont**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [16]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Black Peter [16]

## The recordings

- **gd69-12-04.sbd.wizard.23975.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 16 songs; 119 min; rated 3/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the tape poor-sounding despite an energetic performance; Better sounding than the other copy on the Internet Archive; organ is heard on every song; Sounds much better than the other version, though some tape hiss remains; organ is prominent in the mix [1][5][7][8][9]
- **gd1969-12-04.141723.sbd.fowler.sirmick.flac1644**: soundboard; 14 songs; 119 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer hears tape defects and sound-quality problems in much of the recording apart from Dark Star [12]
- **gd69-12-04.sbd.cotsman.9496.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 119 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [3]

## Around the show

- Garcia had already switched to a Fender Stratocaster by this show [14]
- Thursday show during the distracted run-up to Altamont; short and ragged to start [15]
- Early versions of Workingman's Dead songs make it a classic late-1969 show; Altamont connection noted [8]
- The taping compendium reportedly dismisses the show, but this reviewer finds it not that bad [13]
- Opens December 1969; Workingman's Dead material replaces older songs, hinting at the January 1970 sound while still sounding like the sixties [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-12-04.sbd.wizard.23975.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by The Wizard; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Upgrade from an unnamed benefactor, edited and mastered by The Wizard, with EQ boosting mids and top [1]
- **gd1969-12-04.141723.sbd.fowler.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Julian Fowler; transferred by SIRMick; source: Source: possibly SBD > cassette > ? > DAT > CD; CD > EAC > WAV > mkwACT > SHN - SHN conversion by Julian Fowler, May 2002; [2]. Also: This SIRMick and Julian Fowler recording is a big improvement over the badly degraded circulating cassette copies [15]
- **gd69-12-04.sbd.cotsman.9496.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Joe Jupille and JCotsman; source: Soundboard [3]
